summary: Steel fire tower erected 1939-40 in Washington State Park; a new tower was erected at a better location in 1956; no source found says whether the tower stands today.

events.note: Erected in 1939-40; the 1940 report gives a 68-foot steel tower
Newspaper gives 70 feet; 1,017 people climbed the tower in June and it was used officially to spot fires
New tower erected at a better location; the source does not say what happened to the earlier tower
FY1981-82: entrance road to the tower relocated
Sold at auction for $2,250; the entry does not say what was sold

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1939 report says the tower was being erected that year and the 1940 report says it was erected, so the build spans 1939-40.

notes_for_editor: Status is unknown. Nothing in the sources says whether the tower stands; the 2013 auction entry does not name the item sold. Heights differ: 67 ft (1939 report), 68 ft (1940 report), 70 ft (1941 newspaper). facts.height_m 20.4 follows the 67-foot figure and the existing record. The site of the 1956 tower and the fate of the 1940 tower are not described. The park's history page (https://www.washingtonstateparkmo.com/history/) describes an octagonal lookout shelter built by CCC Company 1743; that is a shelter, not this fire tower, unless a source ties them. The Missouri Life article was blocked (HTTP 403). The lookout page's photo credit is Bob Frakes with a January 30, 2016 caption date; the record already has that photo, so none was added. The agency today is not sourced; Wikipedia describes the park only as a public recreation area.
